statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Submit written appeal to Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days of rejection, providing rationale and alternative name

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for most corporate incorporations in Alberta, including professional services; however, for marine insurance surveying, a physical address may be mandated by regulatory bodies if applicable
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk; routine compliance checks but unannounced on-site inspections are uncommon for this sector

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal Due Diligence and UBO Documentation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for corporate due diligence

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c. B-9, as amended, including Part 1 incorporation provisions, registered office and share capital requirements, Part 2 director/structure provisions, and Complementary Bodies general governance rules; Alberta Corporate Registry Regulations (AR 119/2001).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation and Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta); a corporation may be incorporated without any initial capital or with unpaid/fully paid share consideration as provided in its articles. No statutory escrow account is required at incorporation, provided the subscribed shares are duly issued and any issued share capital is properly valued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the corporation accept the subscriptions of the persons named in the initial share register for the number of common shares set out opposite each subscriber, credited as fully paid, and that share certificates be issued accordingly; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the corporation be situated at [Registered Office Address] and the corporate seal and minute book be maintained there; FINALLY RESOLVED, that the following officers be appointed: Chief Executive Officer and Corporate Secretary, each to serve until the first shareholders' meeting. The directors authorize such officers to execute all filings and banking instructions necessary to implement these resolutions. Approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-clearance and NUANS Corporate Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via accredited NUANS search provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request through an accredited vendor or the Alberta Corporate Registry online portal. Select a distinctive name that does not conflict with existing corporate names or trademarks. If a named corporation is desired, use the resulting NUANS report to support the Articles of Incorporation. The corporate name must include an acceptable legal element such as Inc., Corp., or Ltd. Alternatively, proceed as a numbered corporation using the registry-assigned number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is flagged as confusingly similar, revise the name and obtain a new NUANS report; if the name reservation lapses, re-submit or request a new search.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation and Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the prescribed Alberta Articles of Incorporation, either on paper or through the online filing portal. Provide the proposed registered office address within Alberta, share structure, and full legal names of the initial directors. Have each director execute the consent to act as director. If the corporation intends to conduct regulated activities such as insurance adjusting, attach any required regulatory endorsements or licence references. Submit all documents in English and verify that the NUANS report is less than 90 days old.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction notice or informal query, amend and refile through the same portal within 30 days; resolve any deficiency before final certificate issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Filing Fee and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the statutory filing fee of CAD 200 (approximately USD 145) using the secure payment method, then receive the electronic Certificate of Incorporation and filed Articles. Download and retain the corporate access code for future registry transactions. Verify the corporation name, jurisdiction, incorporation date, and registry number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not issued because of payment failure, rectify payment and refile; if the certificate is lost, request a certified duplicate through Alberta Corporate Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Governance and First Directors' Meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first directors' meeting or obtain the unanimous written consent of the directors under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). Adopt the first board resolution approving share subscriptions and share issuance, adopt by-laws, ratify the registered office, appoint officers, approve the corporate seal and banking authorities, and authorize all post-incorporation filings. Record the proceedings in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as officer forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director resigns or a quorum issue arises, the incorporator or shareholders may appoint replacement directors by written resolution and obtain fresh consents before officers execute further corporate decisions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and CRA Business Number Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, use the corporate access code to complete the CRA business registration and obtain a Business Number. Register for GST/HST if taxable supplies are expected; open a payroll account if the corporation will have employees; and register with the Alberta Workers' Compensation Board if hiring staff. Provide accurate director and registered office information so all federal and provincial tax links are synchronized.
required_dossiers: Alberta WCB employer account application (if hiring staff)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Number is not activated or accounts are not linked, contact CRA Business Enquiries; update mailing address or ownership details through My Business Account to restore service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Licence for Marine Insurance Surveying
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Insurance Council / Superintendent of Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for the appropriate insurance adjuster licence if the corporation will directly or indirectly adjust marine hull and cargo insurance claims in Alberta. Include the Articles of Incorporation, registry extract, designated licensed adjuster information, and evidence of professional insurance. Where the surveyor only performs physical inspections and does not adjust claims, confirm that no insurance adjuster licence is required; nevertheless, obtain a municipal business licence for any office premises and follow Transport Canada marine safety protocols when conducting vessel boarded surveys.
required_dossiers: Alberta Insurance Council adjuster licence application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the deficiency letter within the prescribed period, amend the declaration, or request reconsideration under the Insurance Act of Alberta.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental, Fire Safety, and Occupational Health Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas; Alberta Fire Commissioner; Alberta Occupational Health and Safety; local municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For a low-impact marine surveying office, determine whether registration or notification is required under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (Alberta). Maintain proper hazardous waste manifests for any marine debris, oily waste, or contaminated cargo samples arising from inspections. Obtain a fire safety inspection and certificate of occupancy if the premises are leased or occupied. Conduct a workplace hazard assessment covering dockside and vessel entry, use of personal flotation devices, and any confined-space procedures. No full environmental impact assessment is ordinarily required for an office-based surveyor.
required_dossiers: Registration or notification under EPEA (if applicable)
Certificate of occupancy or property owner approval
Occupational health and safety policy and hazard assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If environmental clearance is delayed, provide supplementary information to the relevant directorate; if a fire inspection identifies non-compliance, remedy the deficiency and request re-inspection; if an OHS order is issued, file a compliance plan within the statutory response period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Insurance Council and Alberta Environment and Protected Areas; Transport Canada Marine Safety for vessel-board operations; local municipal licensing authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Independent Adjuster Licence (Corporate) under the Alberta Insurance Act and Municipal Business Licence

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Low Impact – a full EIA report is not normally required for a marine insurance surveying office; site-specific registration may apply only if ancillary premises generate hazardous waste beyond domestic thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or VOC emission thresholds apply for an office-based professional service. For vessel inspections, bilge water and oil discharges must comply with the Canada Shipping Act and MARPOL Annex I discharge standards; any collected marine debris, cargo samples, or absorbents containing petroleum residue must be manifested and disposed of under Alberta hazardous waste and waste management regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection certificate and certificate of occupancy required for any leased or owned office premises; structural load inspection required if surveying equipment or archives with unusual weight are installed; Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code compliance required for office and field operations, including fall protection, personal flotation devices, vessel access safety, WHMIS training, and emergency response planning.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada, administered through the Business Registration Online (BRO) portal and My Business Account; corporate registration in Alberta is filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta / Alberta Corporate Registration System).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act or provincially under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, obtaining the Alberta incorporation number. 2) Register with the CRA via Business Registration Online or Form RC1 to obtain the nine-digit Business Number (BN) under the registrant account type; open a GST/HST account (RT) where supplies exceed the small supplier threshold or on voluntary election, a corporate income tax account (RC), an import/export account (RM) with the Canada Border Services Agency if goods are traded, and a payroll account (RP) if employees are engaged. 3) Non-resident foreign entities without a Canadian establishment register directly with the CRA for GST/HST purposes only if they carry on business in Canada and make taxable supplies; otherwise they may apply for an individual BN or use treaty protection. 4) Activate CRA My Business Account / Represent a Client access and enrol for GST/HST electronic filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Canadian business corporations are separate taxpayers liable to federal Part I tax under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and Alberta corporate income tax under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act; no pass-through treatment is available for a corporation; the commercial activity is an export-oriented services business treated as an Alberta permanent establishment for provincial allocation).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate an IRS-type 'check-the-box' classification regime; corporate tax status is statutory. Relevant elections include: (1) GST/HST election under ETA section 156 to treat taxable supplies between closely related corporations as made for nil consideration; (2) ETA section 273 election for nil consideration on certain intra-group supplies; (3) Income Tax Act section 85 corporate rollover election on transfers of property to the corporation; (4) Alberta treaty/non-resident branch elections and the proportionate ITA subsection 219(1) Part XIII.2 rules; and (5) hybrid mismatch elections under ITA section 18.4/18.6 for structured financial arrangements (limited and disallowed where double non-taxation results).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under the Excise Tax Act (Canada); Alberta has no provincial sales tax, so the effective combined indirect tax in Alberta is the federal 5% GST only.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in four consecutive calendar quarters of worldwide taxable supplies (GST/HST small supplier threshold); a non-resident that carries on business in Canada must register if the CAD 30,000 threshold derived from Canadian-derived taxable supplies is exceeded, and may elect to register before reaching the threshold to claim input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, fiscal data API, or digital stamping regime is currently in force in Canada. The CRA permits electronic invoices where they satisfy the documentary requirements of ETA section 169 and the record-keeping obligations of ETA section 286. Large registrants must file GST/HST returns electronically using the GST/HST Internet File Transfer (GST34) web service; the Pan-Canadian E-invoicing Initiative is adopting PEPPOL-based business-to-government e-invoicing on a voluntary basis.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada are zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act. Marine hull and cargo claim inspection and survey services supplied to a non-resident underwriter are zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI (section 7) where: (a) the recipient is a non-resident person who is not registered for GST/HST; (b) the recipient is not in Canada at the time the service is performed; and (c) the service does not relate to real property situated in Canada. Zero-rating is unavailable where the survey is rendered for a person in Canada (a Canadian broker, insured, or registered insurer) or where the CRA determines the service is performed for a person in Canada and is not an exported service; in such cases 5% GST net of input tax credits applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Export Reporting through e-Manifest / Canadian Export Declaration) evidencing physical export and the exporter-of-record status
Bill of Lading (ocean/air waybill) or alternative transport document matching the cargo survey assignment and cargo routing
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank foreign-exchange and SWIFT records evidencing receipt of foreign currency settlement from the non-resident underwriter
Survey appointment contract, marine claim instruction letter, and final survey report identifying the non-resident recipient and the insured cargo/vessel subject matter

GST/HST invoice with the BN/RT number and a signed undertaking or certificate of non-resident status confirming the recipient is not registered and was not in Canada when the surveying service was performed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may reassess GST/HST refunds and net tax for four years from the date of assessment (unlimited for misrepresentation or fraud). Export zero-rating claims are scrutinized against the documentary bundle; missing or conflicting export evidence triggers denial of the zero-rating, reassessment of tax at 5%, recovery of refunds, and interest under ETA section 280. False or overstated refunds attract a penalty equal to the greater of CAD 100 and 25% of the overstated rebate (increased to 50% where made knowingly or under circumstances of gross negligence), plus the general anti-avoidance rules under ITA section 245 and potential prosecution under ETA section 327 for evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), acting alongside the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential bank supervision and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/ATF oversight. Canada operates under the Currency Act with a free-floating exchange rate and has no dedicated foreign exchange control administration; exchange policy is implemented through the Bank of Canada's monetary framework and the Minister of Finance's powers under the Bank Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Both current and capital account transactions are fully convertible; the Canadian dollar floats freely with no statutory requirement for central bank approval on cross-border capital movements or profit repatriation. The only material friction for outbound remittances is the Income Tax Act Part XIII withholding regime: 25% on dividends paid to non-residents, typically reduced to 15% (5% for a corporate parent owning at least 10% of the voting shares) under the Canada-US treaty, and a branch/agency tax of 25% on certain Canadian-source earnings of non-resident insurers. Investment Canada Act non-Canadian control review applies only where a foreign investor acquires control of a Canadian business above the prescribed enterprise value thresholds; a newly incorporated Alberta marine surveyor with nominal share capital will normally be exempt from notification. For a service exporter of marine insurance inspection services, export revenue is generally zero-rated for GST/HST purposes and faces no FX conversion impediment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no export proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio: the effective mandatory conversion rate is 0%, and the statutory retention entitlement is 100%. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation; foreign currency receipts may be held indefinitely in Canadian or offshore accounts. The only binding obligations are disclosure-based: FINTRAC requires every international electronic funds transfer of CAD 10,000 or more to be reported by the financial intermediary through an Electronic Funds Transfer Report (EFTR), and physical cross-border currency movements of CAD 10,000 or more must be declared to the Canada Border Services Agency. The Bank of Canada does not administer any conversion or surrender schedule, so the marine surveyor may maintain a natural USD receivable base without forced conversion.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability as a secondary disbursement rail for small-value survey fees, claim reimbursements, and sub-contractor payments, provided the provider is registered as a money service business (MSB) with FINTRAC and holds a verified MSB registration number. Wise is the leading candidate among the target payment rails; however, under Canadian law there is no EU-style electronic money institution (EMI) licence, and MSBs may not accept deposits, cannot hold escrowed client funds, and carry no CDIC deposit insurance. The digital wallet must therefore be subordinate to a Schedule I bank treasury account, never treated as a primary liquidity depository, and restricted to payment transmission only.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FINTRAC rules permit remote identification using dual-process or credential-based verification, so an in-branch visit is not strictly a statutory mandate; however, major Schedule I banks typically require at least one director or senior signatory to attend an in-person interview at the Alberta corporate banking centre (Calgary or Edmonton), or, alternatively, to be represented by a Canadian-resident authorized signatory holding notarized board resolutions. For a non-resident director of the marine surveyor corporation, the most reliable onboarding path is a physical visit combined with certified true copies of the Certificate of Incorporation, or a remote video interview with a notarized identification package and an Alberta-licensed counsel attestation letter. The physical presence condition is best characterized as bank risk-appetite policy rather than a binding legal mandate, and can be waived for low-risk professional service entities where robust documentary evidence and a Canadian-registered agent are supplied.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated single-purpose entity with no operating history and a narrow marine-cargo surveying mandate
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate bundle: Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Incorporation, Alberta Corporate Registry extract, board resolution authorizing account opening, a detailed business plan listing underwriter counterparties, signed engagement letters from marine insurers, pro-forma financial statements for 24 months, and evidence of the statutory licence or professional accreditation required for the ISIC 5222 / NAICS 488390 scope.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) concentration, triggering enhanced due diligence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Corporate Registry beneficial ownership extract, notarized passport copies and utility-bill proof of address for each 10%+ UBO, a corporate organizational chart, a board minute confirming the ownership structure, a statutory declaration confirming absence of nominee or bearer shares, and a completed bank-issued UBO and source-of-funds questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border counterparty geography involving vessel flag-of-convenience states, offshore brokers, or high-risk shipping registries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Underwriter engagement letters, insurer-approved surveyor credentials, survey protocol contracts, Incoterms or service agreements with each vessel owner and broker, completed counterparty KYC questionnaires, an economic-substance memorandum explaining that funds are used solely for verified marine claims inspections, and a signed sanctions-screening attestation confirming no OFAC, UN, or Canadian Listed Persons exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth mismatch on the opening capital injection from overseas shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription ledger, bank statements tracing wire origin, notarized statutory declaration of lawful source of funds, signed investment declaration, and if applicable an Investment Canada Act affidavit confirming that the investment is below notification/review thresholds; where funds are escrowed, the bank's standard source-of-funds certificate and the corporate share-allotment filing with the Alberta Corporate Registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Licensed profession flagged for potential cash-intensive claims settlements or unverified surveyor certification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certification of registration under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, Alberta Insurance Act adjuster's licence or recognized marine surveyor accreditation (NAMS/AMS or IIMS), professional indemnity (E&O) insurance certificate, an internal AML/ATF policy proving exclusive bank-wire settlement rails for all claims payments, and a copy of the entity's claims-handling procedures manual.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route the injection by SWIFT MT103 from the parent or underwriter bank to the Canadian Schedule I bank's CAD or USD clearing account, referencing the full legal corporate name, the Alberta Corporate Registry number, and a clear remittance narrative such as 'share subscription / capital contribution under the Alberta Business Corporations Act'. Canada does not prescribe a numeric FX purpose code; the bank maps the narrative into SWIFT field 70 (Remittance Information) and the ordering institution details into field 50K/52A. The receiving bank will automatically file FINTRAC EFT reports for any international transfer of CAD 10,000 or more. If the investor is a non-Canadian person, a pre-closing analysis under the Investment Canada Act should confirm that no notification or net-benefit review is triggered, and Statistics Canada's quarterly balance-of-payments survey and the Alberta corporate share-allotment filing should be completed in parallel to evidence the true capital injection purpose.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for survey fee disbursements, claim payments to vessel owners, salvors, and cargo interests, and premium refunds to underwriters; for high-value equipment repair or vessel purchase advances, an irrevocable confirmed commercial letter of credit issued by a Canadian Schedule I bank in USD provides the required documentary security. Domestic CAD obligations settle via Payments Canada's Large Value Transfer System for high-value payments and the new Real-Time Rail for retail transfers, while USD-denominated payments clear through the bank's own correspondent banking network in the United States. Every outbound international EFT of CAD 10,000 or more is reported to FINTRAC, and the entity must screen all beneficiaries against Canadian, OFAC, UN, and EU sanctions lists, maintain a wire-only disbursement policy, and reconcile all outgoing payments against the signed survey authorization and underwriter claim file before transmission.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable CAD/USD foreign exchange forwards under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Canadian Schedule I bank dealing desk
FX swaps involving simultaneous spot and forward exchange of CAD/USD principal for periodic premium settlement alignment
Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS) for long-dated USD-denominated claim receivables or dual-currency balance-sheet exposure
European-style vanilla FX options (puts and calls) to hedge contingent large-loss exposures in USD claim settlements

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible in Canada's OTC derivatives market but are commercially suboptimal because the CAD is fully convertible and a deep deliverable CAD/USD forward market exists; NDFs should be used only where the banking counterparty cannot physically deliver USD

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within one (1) month after each anniversary of incorporation, amalgamation, or registration in Alberta; alternatively, no later than March 31 for calendar-year aligned registrants
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee CAD 100; failure for one (1) year or longer may trigger administrative dissolution without court order

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and Alberta Corporate Tax Return (AT1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Alberta Finance (Tax and Revenue Administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six (6) months after the corporation’s fiscal year-end; in all cases no later than the calendar-year requirement for each taxation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of balance owing plus 1% per full month (maximum 12 months); repeated failure may incur higher penalties and criminal proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit required if the corporation is a distributing corporation or if shareholders holding at least 5% of issued shares provide written notice requiring an audit; otherwise, a private non-distributing corporation may waive the appointment of an auditor by unanimous shareholder consent
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private corporations under the CPA Canada Handbook

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually confirm directors and registered office via the Alberta Annual Return; maintain and update the Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) within 15 days of any share transfer or change in ownership, and make it available for inspection by regulators
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 3,500 - 12,000 USD per annum (CAD 4,800 - 16,500) if audit is not waived

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal general corporate income tax rate: 15%. Alberta general corporate income tax rate: 8%. Combined general rate: 23%. A qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation may generally access a 9% federal small-business rate and a 2% Alberta small-business rate on eligible active business income within applicable business limits, producing an effective combined rate of approximately 11%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The federal and Alberta small-business deductions may apply to qualifying active business income of a CCPC, generally subject to the federal and Alberta business limits and associated-corporation rules. The federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development regime, investment tax credits, capital cost allowance, and other generally applicable incentives may apply only if statutory conditions are met. No general corporate income tax holiday applies to a marine insurance surveyor. A non-CCPC or a corporation controlled by non-residents generally cannot claim the CCPC small-business rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, including applicable schedules, filed electronically through CRA-certified tax software under the Corporation Internet Filing program. Alberta AT1 Alberta Corporate Income Tax Return is generally filed electronically through approved software or the CRA corporate tax filing channel. A corporation with a permanent establishment in Alberta generally files both federal and Alberta corporate returns.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 and AT1 are generally due within six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end. Any corporate income tax balance is generally due two months after year-end, or three months after year-end for a qualifying CCPC meeting the statutory conditions. Tax instalments may be required monthly or quarterly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business number, taxation year, fiscal period, address, corporation type, province of permanent establishment, and status as a CCPC or non-CCPC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the corporation's Canadian legal name and business number. Report all Canadian permanent establishments and identify foreign ownership and control accurately. A non-resident-owned Canadian subsidiary is generally a Canadian-resident corporation for Canadian income tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting net income or loss to taxable income or loss, including non-deductible expenses, book depreciation, capital cost allowance, reserves, meals and entertainment, and other tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude non-Canadian accounting amounts that do not relate to the Canadian corporation or its Canadian permanent establishment. Apply Canadian deductibility rules rather than the accounting treatment or tax rules of the parent jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital cost allowance by class, additions, dispositions, undepreciated capital cost, and recapture or terminal loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only depreciable property owned or used by the Canadian corporation or Canadian permanent establishment. Maintain asset-level records, acquisition invoices, disposal documentation, and business-use support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related and associated corporations, ownership percentages, and allocation of the federal business limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose relevant foreign-parent, sister-company, and controlled-corporation relationships. Foreign ownership does not by itself establish CCPC status, but control rights and shareholder agreements must be reviewed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 23 or applicable small-business deduction schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of the federal small-business deduction and eligible active business income where the corporation qualifies as a CCPC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim the CCPC deduction unless Canadian-resident and control requirements are satisfied. Income from services performed in Canada must be separated from foreign-source income and tested under the relevant rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholder information, including specified shareholders and ownership information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report foreign corporate shareholders, individuals, trusts, and ownership percentages as required. Keep beneficial ownership records consistent with corporate registers, anti-money-laundering files, and transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 21 and foreign reporting schedules, if applicable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign income, foreign tax credits, foreign affiliates, and other cross-border tax attributes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Canadian corporation with foreign affiliates, foreign property, foreign branches, or foreign tax paid must test applicable schedules and information returns separately. Foreign withholding tax cannot be claimed automatically as a credit without statutory support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Alberta AT1 General Information and Tax Calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta taxable income, Alberta allocation, Alberta tax rate, small-business deduction, credits, instalments, balance payable, and refunds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income to Alberta using the applicable corporate allocation rules and report Alberta permanent-establishment activity. A corporation operating in multiple provinces must complete the required allocation schedules and cannot allocate all Canadian income to Alberta solely because its registered office is there.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 23 or T106, as applicable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information concerning non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents, including payments, receipts, loans, management fees, royalties, interest, insurance-related services, and property transfers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report qualifying non-arm's-length cross-border transactions in Canadian dollars using consistent exchange-rate records. Match T106 amounts to the general ledger, withholding slips, invoices, agreements, and transfer-pricing records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing generally attracts the greater of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% of unpaid tax for each full month late, up to 12 months, or an increased penalty where a demand to file has been issued. Alberta may impose comparable late-filing penalties under its corporate tax legislation. Arrears interest is compounded daily at prescribed rates. Failure to pay instalments can trigger instalment interest and penalties. False statements or omissions may result in a penalty generally equal to 50% of the understated tax or improperly claimed credit, with gross-negligence, tax-evasion, and criminal consequences in serious cases.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax on taxable dividends paid or credited by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident, subject to treaty reduction. Common treaty outcomes include 5% where the beneficial owner is a qualifying corporate shareholder meeting ownership thresholds and 15% for other qualifying treaty residents. The Canada-United States treaty commonly provides 5% for a qualifying 10% corporate shareholder and 15% otherwise.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Confirm that the recipient is the beneficial owner, resident in a treaty jurisdiction, and entitled to treaty benefits. Obtain and retain a valid certificate of residence or equivalent reliable evidence, ownership and beneficial-ownership documentation, treaty eligibility analysis, and applicable limitation-on-benefits evidence. Apply the reduced rate at source only where the payer has reasonable grounds to believe the treaty conditions are satisfied. Otherwise withhold 25%, remit to the CRA by the prescribed deadline, and issue NR4 information slips. Treaty relief does not generally require advance CRA approval, but the payer must support its determination and may face liability for deficient withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Part XIII rate is generally 25% for royalties and interest paid or credited to non-residents, subject to exemptions and treaty reductions. Treaty royalty rates commonly range from 0% to 10%, depending on the treaty and royalty category. Interest paid to an arm's-length non-resident is generally exempt from Part XIII withholding, except for specified categories such as participating debt interest; non-arm's-length interest is generally subject to 25% unless reduced or exempted by treaty. Management, technical, and service fees may be subject to withholding under separate rules where the services are rendered in Canada, including the statutory 15% Regulation 105 withholding regime for certain services performed in Canada by non-residents.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada has no general monetary threshold below which contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation is automatically unnecessary. The Income Tax Act requires reasonable efforts to determine arm's-length prices and conditions. Form T106 generally applies where aggregate reportable non-arm's-length non-resident transactions exceed CAD 1 million, subject to statutory rules and exclusions. A Canadian Local File is generally expected under the OECD-aligned documentation framework where applicable, while a Master File and country-by-country reporting generally apply to multinational enterprise groups meeting the CAD-equivalent EUR 750 million consolidated-revenue threshold under the Canadian CbC rules. The CAD 1 million T106 threshold is not a safe harbor from transfer-pricing documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have a separate general Economic Substance Regulation regime equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. Substance is assessed through the transfer-pricing arm's-length principle, beneficial-ownership rules, the general anti-avoidance rule, specific anti-avoidance provisions, residence and central-management considerations, and business-purpose and factual-control analysis. A Canadian corporation conducting marine claims inspection should maintain qualified personnel, operational decision-making, client contracts, survey reports, insurance coverage, books and records, and commercially supportable pricing in Alberta or another genuine operating location. A shell entity with no personnel, functions, risks, or decision-making authority may face denied deductions, recharacterization, withholding exposure, penalties, and reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Deliberate False Reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing Canadian revenue, fabricating survey expenses, suppressing cash receipts, overstating deductible intercompany charges, using false invoices, or knowingly filing materially false T2 or AT1 returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil reassessment of tax, arrears interest, gross-negligence penalties generally equal to 50% of the understated tax or improperly claimed credit, and prosecution for tax evasion. Criminal tax-evasion penalties may include a fine of 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment for up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may face personal criminal liability where they participated in or authorized the conduct. The corporate veil is not routinely pierced for ordinary corporate income tax debts, but personal liability can arise through statutory director-liability provisions, knowing participation, fraud, dishonest conduct, or separate civil claims. Travel restrictions are not an automatic tax penalty but may arise from criminal process, bail conditions, or enforcement orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File or Pay Corporate Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Late T2 or AT1 filing, failure to remit instalments, failure to pay assessed tax, or repeated non-compliance after a CRA or Alberta demand to file.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late-filing penalties, instalment penalties, daily-compounded arrears interest, collection actions, garnishment, liens, seizure, and potential prosecution for failure to file. Repeated demand-to-file failures can produce enhanced penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors generally are not personally liable merely because corporate income tax remains unpaid. Personal exposure may arise for source deductions, GST/HST, and certain other trust amounts if the corporation failed to remit and the director did not exercise due diligence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificial royalties, interest, management fees, insurance-related service charges, or cost allocations that lack commercial substance or exceed arm's-length pricing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income reassessment, denial or reduction of deductions, withholding-tax reassessment, potential transfer-pricing penalties generally equal to 10% of the relevant adjustment where statutory conditions are met, interest, and extended reassessment periods in certain cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal exposure for knowingly participating in fraudulent arrangements or approving false records. Ordinary transfer-pricing adjustments normally remain corporate liabilities unless separate misconduct or statutory liability is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting or misstating T106 information, foreign affiliate information, related-party loans, non-resident payments, or treaty-based withholding positions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Information-return penalties, withholding-tax liability, interest, reassessment, and penalties for failure to provide requested books, records, or contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for source deductions or other trust amounts and may incur criminal exposure if the omission was knowingly fraudulent. A documentation failure alone generally does not pierce the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper Treaty Relief and Beneficial-Ownership Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying reduced withholding rates through conduit entities, false residence certificates, treaty shopping, nominee arrangements, or failure to verify beneficial ownership and treaty eligibility.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of underwithheld Part XIII tax, interest, penalties, denial of treaty benefits under applicable anti-abuse provisions, and potential application of the general anti-avoidance rule. The payer may remain liable even where the recipient received the payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may face personal criminal or civil exposure for knowingly false certifications, fraud, or deliberate withholding failures. Statutory director liability is strongest for remittance obligations and trust amounts rather than ordinary corporate tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to withhold or remit payroll deductions, failure to remit GST/HST collected from clients, or treating collected taxes as corporate working capital.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Trust recovery, prescribed interest, remittance penalties, assessments, director-liability proceedings, garnishment, liens, and criminal prosecution in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be jointly and severally personally liable for certain unremitted source deductions and GST/HST, subject to statutory due-diligence defenses and limitation periods. This is a principal personal-liability risk for directors of an Alberta corporation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal Alberta corporation that has no real personnel, operational capability, client control, survey expertise, records, or risk assumption, while booking Canadian revenue or deducting offshore charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of income and expenses, denial of deductions, transfer-pricing adjustments, treaty denial, withholding assessments, interest, penalties, and possible corporate-residence or permanent-establishment disputes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal exposure may arise where directors knowingly use the entity to mislead tax authorities, commit fraud, or evade statutory remittances. Mere use of a limited-liability corporation for legitimate business does not itself create personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed or Misrepresented Marine Insurance Survey Activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Performing regulated insurance-adjusting or claims-handling functions without required provincial authorization, misrepresenting qualifications, or issuing inaccurate survey reports used for insurance claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Provincial licensing sanctions, administrative penalties, cease-and-desist orders, professional or regulatory discipline, civil damages, contract disputes, and potential criminal consequences for fraud or false documentation. Tax deductions and insurance payments may be challenged where records are fabricated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers may face personal civil or criminal exposure for fraud, knowing misrepresentation, professional misconduct, or authorization of unlawful operations. Limited liability generally does not protect intentional torts or criminal conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting suspicious claim-related funds, failing to identify beneficial owners, structuring payments, ignoring sanctions indicators, or using Wise or wire transfers to disguise payment origin or destination.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC compliance penalties, reporting failures, administrative monetary penalties, account restrictions, seizure or forfeiture, criminal prosecution, and sanctions-related penalties under applicable Canadian law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may face personal liability or criminal charges where they direct, authorize, facilitate, or knowingly ignore money laundering or sanctions violations. Corporate status does not shield deliberate participation.
